                                          Hierarchical Long Video Understanding with Audiovisual Entity Cohesion and
                                                                       Agentic Search

arXiv:2601.13719v2 [cs.CV] 24 Mar 2026
                                                                    Abstract

                                         Long video understanding presents significant challenges
                                         for vision-language models due to extremely long con-
                                         text windows. Existing solutions relying on naive chunk-
                                         ing strategies with retrieval-augmented generation, typi-
                                         cally suffer from information fragmentation and a loss of
                                         global coherence. We present HAVEN, a unified frame-
                                         work for long-video understanding that enables coherent
                                         and comprehensive reasoning by integrating audiovisual
                                         entity cohesion and hierarchical video indexing with agen-
                                         tic search. First, we preserve semantic consistency by in-
                                         tegrating entity-level representations across visual and au-
                                                                                                         Figure 1. The proposed hierarchical video indexing with audiovi-
                                         ditory streams, while organizing content into a structured      sual entity cohesion and agentic search.
                                         hierarchy spanning global summary, scene, segment, and
                                         entity levels. Then we employ an agentic search mechanism
                                         to enable dynamic retrieval and reasoning across these          multiple entities, dynamic interactions, and evolving mul-
                                         layers, facilitating coherent narrative reconstruction and      timodal signals makes coherent interpretation and entity
                                         fine-grained entity tracking. Extensive experiments demon-      tracking particularly difficult.
                                         strate that our method achieves good temporal coherence,           Recent advances in large Vision-Language Models
                                         entity consistency, and retrieval efficiency, establishing a    (VLMs) have led to substantial progress on short-video
                                         new state-of-the-art with an overall accuracy of 84.1% on       tasks such as captioning, question answering, and tempo-
                                         LVBench. Notably, it achieves outstanding performance in        ral grounding, yet their application to long videos remains
                                         the challenging reasoning category, reaching 80.1%. These       constrained by limited context windows and computational
                                         results highlight the effectiveness of structured, multimodal   bottlenecks. To mitigate these issues, techniques such as
                                         reasoning for comprehensive and context-consistent under-       adaptive sampling [9, 12, 30], and token compression [15,
                                         standing of long-form videos.                                   21, 22, 25] are proposed, enabling longer sequences under
                                                                                                         resource limits. Memory-based approaches [5, 8] further
                                                                                                         extend temporal coverage by dynamically retaining and up-
                                         1. Introduction                                                 dating salient information. While these techniques improve
                                                                                                         scalability, they often sacrifice critical details or contexts,
                                         The rapid growth of long-form video content in domains
                                                                                                         and struggle to preserve the semantic continuity across dis-
                                         such as entertainment, education, and surveillance poses
                                                                                                         tant segments.
                                         significant challenges for automated understanding sys-
                                                                                                            To address these issues, recent methods increasingly
                                         tems. Unlike short clips, hour-long videos demand rea-
                                                                                                         adopt retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) [10, 13, 19,
                                         soning over tens of thousands of frames and audio streams,
                                                                                                         20, 29] to dynamically fetch relevant video segments,
                                         where events unfold across extended durations and depend
                                                                                                         alongside agentic frameworks [4, 24, 31] that autonomously
                                         on subtle cross-scene relationships. The interleaving of
                                                                                                         plan and reason over the video content. However, both

nals (e.g., clip-level captions), which yields fragmented or      approaches [5, 8] dynamically retain and update salient con-
redundant evidence and severely weakens global narrative          tent, extending the temporal receptive field and support-
coherence. Second, the absence of a hierarchical video rep-       ing reasoning over longer durations. In addition, other ap-
resentation deprives agents of the structural context needed      proaches such as LongVLM [27] and VideoStreaming [18]
for multi-level reasoning. Consequently, models can only          leverage hierarchical token aggregation and memory propa-
resort to inefficient, multi-round retrievals to recover cross-   gation with global-local semantics to support scalable long
segment continuity, introducing unnecessary complexity.           video understanding. Despite these advances, existing solu-
    In this paper, we propose a unified agentic framework         tions struggle to balance global coherence with local detail,
that shifts long-video understanding from fragmented re-          making it difficult to reason across distant scenes or main-
trieval to coherent, structured comprehension (see Fig. 1).       tain entity continuity over time.
Our approach is based on two core innovations: audiovi-
sual entity cohesion and hierarchical indexing. First, we in-     RAG-based Long Video Understanding RAG has

ploit speaker identity cues as a powerful yet often over-         eral directions, including aligned video-text chunking [10],
looked signal for entity consolidation, serving as an ef-         graph-based entity semantics [19], omni-contextual adap-
fective “glue” for maintaining long-range entity coherence.       tive selection [29], and temporal dependency modeling
The resulting entity representations provide reliable build-      [20]. However, their reliance on fragmented segments and
ing blocks for higher-level scene interpretation as well. Sec-    lack of global context limit temporal coherence, thus mak-
ond, we construct a hierarchical database that organizes          ing complex reasoning tasks challenging.
video content at multiple granularities, i.e. global summary,
scene, segment, and entity, enabling flexible and multi-level     Long Video Agents Unlike static RAG-based retrieval,
retrieval. Built atop this hierarchy, our agentic search mech-    recent work leverages LLMs as autonomous agents for it-
anism supports goal-driven reasoning across granularities.        erative planning, retrieval, and reasoning over long videos,
Ultimately, by integrating these components, our frame-           enabling dynamic interaction through tool use and struc-
work achieves scalable and holistic long-video understand-        tured search. Representative works include VideoAgent
ing. Our contributions are summarized as follows:                 [24], which treats LLMs as agents that iteratively retrieve

2. Related Work                                                   Hierarchical Video Representation Long video under-
                                                                  standing often requires modeling local-global context and
Long Video Understanding with large VLMs Large                    hierarchical relationships across scenes, segments, and en-
vision-language models have been extended to long-form            tities. Prior works address this via local-global aggrega-
video tasks using techniques such as adaptive sampling            tion [18, 27], tree-based structure [26], and graph-based re-
[9, 12, 30] and token compression [15, 21, 22, 25], which         trieval [19, 29], while [31] tracks subjects in a global reg-
reduce token overhead by selecting salient frames or merg-        istry. Although these methods improve semantic coherence,
ing redundant information across time and modality. These         some models incur high online computation and lack a uni-
strategies enable longer sequence processing under mem-           fied offline hierarchical index spanning video, scene, seg-
ory and compute constraints but often sacrifice critical de-      ment, and entity levels, which is a core feature of our frame-
tails or incur additional online computation. Memory-based        work for efficient and coherent long video reasoning.

E. Efficiency
Our semantic-consistent hierarchy enables more efficient
navigation, achieving higher accuracy with fewer reason-
ing steps and less runtime compared with DVD, as shown
in Table 4.

F. Proprietary models
Our API versions are GPT-4.1 (2025-04-14) and o3 (2025-
04-16). Variance of three runs on LVBench is 0.149, which
demonstrates the robustness of our method. Furthermore,
Our method achieves an competitive accuracy of 75.8% on
Table 5. The agentic search prompt structure. The prompt is divided into four distinct sections: goal, tools, tool preferences and hints.

Module             Prompt Content

GOAL               You will be given a set of tools to assist you exploring the video, understanding it and reasoning the answer.
                   Please follow the THINK → ACT → OBSERVE loop:
                   • THOUGHT: Reason step-by-step about what question to ask and which tool to call next.
                   • ACTION: Call exactly one tool that moves you closer to the final answer.
                   • OBSERVATION: Summarize the tool call’s output.
                   Continue the loop until the user’s query is fully resolved, then end your turn with the final answer.

TOOLS              Here are tools you can use to reveal your reasoning process whenever the provided information is insufficient:
                   • global scene browse tool: for scene-related query to explore scenarios, temporal orders, and contextual structure
                   in a rough manner without precise details (e.g., first appearance, second song, third collision).
                   • entity search tool: for entity-related information retrieval, finding important subjects involved in events.
                   • clip caption search wtime tool: to search from rough captions and audio transcriptions of local clips within a list
                   of time ranges related to a query. If you want to search from the whole video, use the whole video time range.
                   • clip visual search wtime tool: to search from visual features of local clips within a list of time ranges
                   (list[tuple[HH:MM:SS, HH:MM:SS]]) related to a query. If you want to search from the whole video,
                   use the whole video time range. This tool may provide more detailed information as a supplement to
                   clip caption search wtime tool.
                   • clip caption inspect tool: to extract rough captions and audio transcriptions of local clips within any list of time
                   ranges (list[tuple[HH:MM:SS, HH:MM:SS]]). This tool is suitable for further inspecting what happened in a time
                   range before or after some events happened.
                   • visual inspect tool: to extract details from local visual clips within a narrow list of time ranges that covers less than
                   50 seconds to answer a question or retrieve query-related details. When the time ranges cover over 50 seconds, first
                   use clip caption inspect tool to get a rough context.
                   • finish: Once you believe you have found the answer, you can call the finish tool with an answer.

TOOL PREF-         • When no context is given, call global scene browse tool for scene-related queries to get an overview of related
ERENCES            context and timelines,
                   or call clip caption search wtime tool for event-related queries to get a rough context and timelines,
                   or call entity search tool for entity-related queries.
                   • When you cannot locate the needed context from scene or entity tools, use clip caption search wtime tool or
                   clip visual search wtime tool to expand your search.
                   • If the retrieved material by clip caption search wtime tool lacks relevant contexts, further call
                   clip visual search wtime tool for more fine-grained search.
                   • If the retrieved material lacks precise, question-relevant detail (e.g., an unknown name, count) or you are uncertain
                   of an answer after searching, call clip caption inspect tool
                   or inspect frames with visual inspect tool with a list of time ranges to take a closer look.
                   • After locating an answer in the script, always make a CONFIRM with visual inspect tool query.

HINTS              • Before giving the final answer, confirm critical visual or numeric facts with visual inspect tool.
                   • If you call clip caption search wtime tool in three consecutive times but still cannot find useful information to
                   answer the question, please try clip visual search wtime tool to get more detailed information.
                   • You have at most 10 iterations of THINK→ACT→OBSERVE; plan strategically. Avoid redundant information
                   retrieval steps.
                   • To make a good plan to questions that need complex reasoning, sometimes you need to first ask some other related
                   contexts instead of directly asking the target question,
                   • For questions that need counting the number of times an event occurs over time, call global scene browse tool first.
                   If you are uncertain about its answer, please search for related events or subjects without counting first to find all
                   related information, then do the counting based on observations.
                   • Your final answer must be concise and directly address the question.
